theme: Sing to the LORD; declare his glory among the nations
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 96. You met it earlier as the song David sang when the ark came to Jerusalem. Read it now as a missionary hymn: it calls God’s people to declare his glory among the nations.
settingTheScene: Psalm 96 is almost identical to the song in 1 Chronicles 16 that David appointed when the ark entered Jerusalem. In the Psalter, it begins a group of psalms (96 to 99) that celebrate the kingship of the LORD over the nations. Following Paul’s farewell to the Ephesians, this psalm turns our attention outward again: the mission is not finished, and the church is called to declare his glory to all peoples.
observation: “Oh sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth!” (v. 1).
“Sing to the LORD, bless his name; tell of his salvation from day to day” (v. 2).
“Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples!” (v. 3).
“For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods” (v. 4).
“For all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols, but the LORD made the heavens” (v. 5).
“Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth!” (v. 9).
“Say among the nations, The LORD reigns!” (v. 10).
“For he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples in his faithfulness” (v. 13).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a new song. The call is to the whole earth. The church has sung new songs in each generation, because each generation experiences God’s salvation afresh. “Tell of his salvation from day to day.” Day by day, the people of God are to speak of what he has done.

Then the center of the psalm: “Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples!” This is a missions command in the Psalms. Israel was a priestly kingdom, not only to keep the faith but to declare it to the world. Why? Because the LORD is great and greatly to be praised. The gods of the peoples are worthless idols, a word that sounds like “nothings,” but the LORD made the heavens. Idols cannot save. The nations need to know the living God.

Verses 7 to 9 call the families of the peoples to ascribe to the LORD glory and strength, to bring an offering and come into his courts. Worship is the right response of every nation. The splendor of holiness is the beauty of God’s character, before which all should tremble.

Verse 10 gives the message: “Say among the nations, The LORD reigns!” This is the gospel in the Old Testament. The reign of God is news. He has established the world; it shall never be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity. This is not a threat but good news to the oppressed. All creation joins in: the heavens are glad, the earth rejoices, the sea roars, the fields exult, and the trees of the forest sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes.

The psalm ends with the coming of the LORD to judge the earth in righteousness and in his faithfulness. For Christians, this coming is the return of Christ. We tell the nations of his salvation and his coming, and invite them to be reconciled to him before that day. The tone of the psalm is joy, because the coming judge is the same one who has saved.
connection: 1 Chronicles 16:23-33 gives the same song at the bringing of the ark. Psalm 67, 97, 98, and 99 are related psalms. Isaiah 42:10-12 also calls for a new song. Isaiah 52:7-10 proclaims the reign of God. Psalm 115:3-8 mocks idols. 1 Thessalonians 1:9 says they turned from idols to serve a living God. Revelation 5:9, 14:3, and 15:3-4 contain the new song. Matthew 28:18-20 is the Great Commission.
application:
Sing or read a hymn or song today that you have never used before. Make it a new song.

Tell someone of his salvation today. Say a sentence about what God has done for you.

Say verse 10 aloud, “The LORD reigns!” over a situation that troubles you.
prayerPrompts: Sing to the LORD a new song, in your own words.
Tell someone of his salvation today, or ask him to help you.
Declare his glory among the nations.
